This is intentionally a subset, not the full export. Each retained issue value
is copied byte-for-byte from the original response (including all releases and
repository versions); only surrounding source-package dictionaries were rebuilt,
with a terminal newline. No status, version, urgency, description or date was
manufactured. The original full response is not committed.

Selected source-package/issue pairs:
  openssh / CVE-2024-6387: bookworm resolved, fixed 1:9.2p1-2+deb12u3.
  openssh / CVE-2024-6409: resolved with fixed_version "0" (not affected).
  openssh / CVE-2026-59995: bookworm open, no-DSA Minor issue, postponed.
  angular.js / CVE-2026-27970: bookworm undetermined.
  adduser / TEMP-0331720-9168FE: provisional tracker identifier, not a CVE.
  389-ds-base / CVE-2016-5416: bookworm open with unimportant urgency.

Backport corroboration:
https://www.debian.org/security/2024/dsa-5724
redirects to the actual announcement:
https://lists.debian.org/debian-security-announce/2024/msg00135.html
DSA-5724-1, July 01 2024, states that stable/bookworm CVE-2024-6387 is
fixed in 1:9.2p1-2+deb12u3. This is a Debian revision backport, not an upstream
OpenSSH semantic-version range. The parser uses the export's source package
openssh and fixed_version, never the newer repositories entries. Native installed
predecessor/successor versions in tests are explicit test inputs, not extra vendor
records. Matchers must use inventory SourceName and SourceVersion for binaries
such as openssh-server; no binary name/version map is inferred from this export.

Not-affected corroboration:
https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2024-6409
states "openssh <not-affected> (Exploitable issue in RHEL9 packaged versions)".
A resolved fixed_version of "0" is a not-affected assertion for this record, not a
literal installed-version threshold and not evidence that the entire package is
safe from other issues. No architecture scope is published in this JSON export.

Vendor semantics and release mapping:
https://security-team.debian.org/security_tracker.html
https://www.debian.org/releases/
https://salsa.debian.org/security-tracker-team/security-tracker/-/raw/master/lib/python/security_db.py
The source's calculateJson method selects source_package_status/source_packages,
produces open/resolved/undetermined, emits fixed_version only for resolved entries,
and chooses base/security/LTS repository states. Package versions in repositories
are archive observations, not the first version fixing a vulnerability.
11=bullseye, 12=bookworm, 13=trixie are explicit numeric release mappings. Mutable
stable/oldstable aliases and future testing releases are not inferred. This
acquired export contains bookworm, trixie, forky and sid, not bullseye. A mapped
release missing entirely from the input must fail rather than become a clean feed.

No-DSA, ignored and postponed annotations describe the vendor's update policy,
not non-vulnerability: open entries remain affected without a known fix.
Historical low/medium/high urgency is retained through the shared normalizer;
not yet assigned/end-of-life becomes unknown severity. Unimportant is retained as
negligible, not treated as a blanket clean assertion: the vendor also uses it for
packages not covered by security support. Undetermined is an explicit unknown
assessment, not an open confirmed vulnerability or a safe package. Unknown status
and unsupported constraint fields fail closed. Provisional TEMP identifiers are
preserved as advisory IDs without inventing CVE aliases.

Coverage and time caveats:
The full export is much broader than the DSA-only OSV records, but does not prove
complete inventory coverage. It emits tracked issues for source packages in
supported releases, not an authenticated package universe or inventory-specific
binary/source mapping; removed/untracked source packages and unsupported suites
cannot be declared clean by absence. Both full exports and selected imports remain
partial coverage in this implementation. No current export can certify the
absence of undiscovered or not-yet-triaged vulnerabilities.
The JSON has no publication date, modification date, generated-at timestamp,
snapshot signature or acquisition timestamp. Advisory published_at remains absent;
neither the CVE year, DSA announcement date nor acquisition clock is substituted.
HTTPS authenticates acquisition but does not make a previously cached vendor
export current. Local checked_at/max_age measures local acquisition age only;
HTTP Last-Modified/Age observed above are distinct transport metadata and are not
record publication dates. Air-gap custody and capture age require separate trusted
operator evidence. These fixtures establish parser behavior, not current live
vulnerability coverage, signature verification, or executed test results.
